newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia lupin disease problem deepens-ABARE.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia lupin disease problem deepens-ABARE.

text.p: Australia's production of lupins is expected to fall by 10 percent to 1.3 million tonnes in 1996/97 and a moratorium on plantings was expected to be imposed until 1998 due to an outbreak of anthracnose disease, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics said.
ABARE said in its latest Australian Crop report that anthracnose disease had broken out in the Western Australian (WA) and South Australian (SA) lupin crops.
ABARE said the number of properties with anthracnose discoveries has continued to rise and the disease had also spread from albus lupins to a new lupin variety in both WA and SA.
The outbreak of anthracnose disease continues to cause concern among lupin growers, ABARE said.
"At this stage, over 90 properties have been reported to have been affected by the disease in WA," it said.
In its previous report issued October 22, ABARE said the disease was considered under control with 54 properties infected.
While albus (white) lupins have been most severely affected, anthracnose has also been reported in angustifolius lupins on several properties, ABARE said.
To prevent further outbreaks, a moratorium on the planting of albus lupins in most locations was likely until 1998, it said.
In SA, anthracnose had been found in angustifolius lupins on nine properties on the southern Eyre peninsula, it said.
The total area affected so far was 550 hectares, it said.
Good rains throughtout the WA wheatbelt in late October had improved yield prospects, ABARE also said.
Despite the anthracnose problem, lupin production in SA was still expected to increase by 11 percent in 1996/97 to 80,000 tonnes, ABARE said.

ABARE's latest estimate for total Australian lupin production in 1996/97 is 1.281 million tonnes, up from the previous estimate of 1.230 million tonnes but down from 1995/96 production of 1.429 million tonnes.
Lupins are mainly used as stock feed in Australia. The value of the industry in WA is estimated at A$200 million a year.
